summary: This sermon examines James 4:1-10, confronting Christians about divided loyalty between God and the world. Using the biblical language of spiritual adultery, the preacher challenges listeners to recognize how proximity to worldly values creates internal conflict and relationship problems, while proximity to God brings grace, perspective, and restoration.
key_points: Conflicts and quarrels reveal what we're giving allegiance to—God or the world
James calls Christians 'adulterers' for divided loyalty and friendship with the world
God generously gives grace to the humble, not the proud
The solution is drawing near to God through humility and resisting worldly desires
Relational proximity determines perspective—close to God, problems shrink; close to problems, God seems small
big_idea: When we prioritize proximity to God over the world's values, we discover how our problems shrink in the presence of a faithful God who generously offers grace to the humble.
title: Relational Proximity
